A registered Bank of America, NA exposure of 200 against a bank_of_america cap of 100 produces no breach and reports the target missing. The canonical-spelling control produces a fail breach of 100. <!-- auto-status-summary:start -->
## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
`src/counter_risk/ppt/concentration_table.py:86` formats metric cell values in `append_concentration_table_slide` using `f"{float(value):.2%}"` without checking `math.isfinite()`, and without handling `None` values. When metric values contain `None`, `nan`, or `inf`, PPT table slides render raw strings like `"None"`, `"nan%"`, or `"inf%"` into presentation slide cells. In contrast, other PPT report renderers in the codebase format missing or non-finite values as `"-"` or `"N/A"`.

#### Tasks
- [x] In `src/counter_risk/ppt/concentration_table.py`, safely format percentage and numeric values in `append_concentration_table_slide` when encountering `None`, `NaN`, `Inf`, or invalid values.
- [x] In `tests/ppt/test_concentration_table.py`, add unit tests verifying slides render placeholder strings instead of `"nan%"` or `"inf%"` when metrics contain non-finite numbers or `None`.

#### Acceptance criteria
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/ppt/test_concentration_table.py -q` passes; non-finite floats and `None` values render placeholder strings in table cells.
- [x] Direct inspection verifies rendered slide table cells for `float('nan')` contain `"-"` or `"N/A"`.
- [x] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break non-finite handling in `src/counter_risk/ppt/concentration_table.py` by reverting to `f"{float(value):.2%}"`; non-finite PPT test must fail; restore and rerun.

<!-- auto-status-summary:end -->
